preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and len(stdin.split()) == 2 and all(1 <= int(x) <= 2e5 for x in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: Input consists of a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5) followed by n integers a_1, ..., a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 2e10^5).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (all(1 <= int(x) <= 5 for x in stdout.split()) and len(stdout.split()) == n)
postconditions.description: Output is either '-1' (no convenient fingering exists) or a sequence of n integers b_1, ..., b_n (1 ≤ b_i ≤ 5) representing a valid fingering.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and all(1 <= i < n and ((a[i] < a[i+1] and b[i] < b[i+1]) or (a[i] > a[i+1] and b[i] > b[i+1]) or (a[i] == a[i+1] and b[i] != b[i+1])) for i in range(n-1))
postconditions.description: If output is not '-1', then the fingering b_1, ..., b_n satisfies the convenience rules: for all 1 ≤ i < n, if a_i < a_{i+1} then b_i < b_{i+1}, if a_i > a_{i+1} then b_i > b_{i+1}, and if a_i = a_{i+1} then b_i ≠ b_{i+1}. Here, a = list(map(int, stdin.split()[1:])), b = list(map(int, stdout.split())).
